title: Folder sync worker with bounded concurrency
name: Folder sync worker

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code handles asynchronous work and failures during a sync? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
During a sync, three stale remote files are removed and the removal of one of them rejects. What is the effect on the sync call?
choices: sync rejects with that error, and the remaining two removals are cancelled.
sync rejects, but only after the other two removals have finished.
sync resolves normally; the two successful removals are counted in removed, and the failure is reported in removalFailures.
sync resolves, but removed counts all three, because allSettled hides the rejection.

questions.prompt: this.store.recordSync(summary) is called without await and sync() returns the summary right after. Suppose recordSync later rejects. What happens?
choices: The error is logged as a warning and nothing else changes; the caller already has its summary.
Node emits an unhandled rejection, because the promise is not awaited by anyone.
The next call to sync() throws the stored error before doing any work.
The error is thrown inside sync()'s try/catch in run(), so the cycle is reported as failed.

questions.prompt: concurrency is 4 and 20 files need uploading; one file's upload keeps failing and waits for its backoff delays between attempts. How many uploads can be in flight at once, and what happens to the delayed file's slot?
choices: Up to 20, because each worker starts the next upload while the delayed one sleeps.
At most 4; the worker that owns the delayed file stays busy during its retries, so the other three workers handle the remaining files in the meantime.
At most 3 while the delayed file retries, since the sleeping worker is returned to the pool and the pool shrinks.
At most 4, but the delayed file's backoff blocks the Node event loop, so all uploads pause.
